summary: Otto Neugebauer worked in history and archaeology. He studied at Graz, Munich, and Göttingen (PhD ~1926) and under Boris Turayev. He held posts at Göttingen, Copenhagen, Brown University (1939–1969), and the Institute for Advanced Study.

Otto Rosenberg specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Japanology. He studied at St. Petersburg and Bonn under Theodore Stcherbatsky, Sergey Oldenburg, Hermann Jacobi, and Rudolf Lange. He held a professorship at Saint Petersburg State University from 1911 to 1919.

Otto Stein was an Indologist who studied at Charles University (Dr. phil. 1918) under Moriz Winternitz and Heinrich Swoboda. He worked at the Oriental Institute in 1929 and served as ordinary professor at Charles University from 1930 to 1939.

Otto Strauss worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Munich, Berlin, and Kiel (doctoral degree ~1905) under Paul Deussen and Hermann Oldenberg. He held professorships at Calcutta (1913–1920), Kiel (1920), and Breslau (1928–1935).

Otto von Böhtlingk was an Indologist and linguist who studied at St. Petersburg, Berlin, and Bonn under Franz Bopp and Christian Lassen. He served at the Russian Academy of Sciences (director 1849–1868) and the University of Jena (~1868–1885).

Owen Flanagan is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Fordham University (~1966–1970) and Boston University (~1973–1977), and held a post as Professor of Philosophy at Duke University (~1996).

P. A. Payutto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~1957–1962), where he served as Associate Dean (~1964–1973), and held a post at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara in 1995.
P. B. Annangaracharya worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Asuri Ramanujacharya and served as Head Pandit at Sanskrit Pathashala, Vadtal (attested 1954).
P. B. Meegaskumbura is a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies who held a post as professor at the University of Ceylon, attested in 1991 and 2010.

P. D. Premasiri works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Ceylon, Cambridge, and Hawaiʻi (PhD 1980) under several scholars including David J. Kalupahana. He held various academic posts at the University of Ceylon from 1963 to 2010.
P. H. Joshi is an Indologist who served as a Research Officer at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara, attested between 1976 and 1988, with affiliation further attested in 2002.

P. K. Mukhopadhyay worked in philosophy and Indology. He served as Professor of Philosophy at Jadavpur University and was a National Fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research, attested in 2009.

P. N. Pattabhirama Sastri was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under A. Chinnaswami Sastri (~1928–1934). He held posts at Banaras Hindu University (~1935–1942) and as Reader in Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (~1956–1967).

P. P. Subrahmanya Sastri was an Indologist who studied at Madras and Oxford. He served as Curator at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library (attested 1937) and Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Presidency College (attested 1937–1944).

P. Pratap Kumar is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held a professorship at the University of KwaZulu-Natal (attested 2010) and was a visiting professor at Colorado College (attested 2010).
P. S. Chandrasekharan is an Indologist who studied as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi, attested in 2026.

P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Bishop Heber College and the University of Madras (Ph.D.). He held posts at Bishop Heber College, Rajah's College, and Annamalai University (1942–1947).
P. Swaminathan is an Indologist who earned an M.Litt. at the University of Madras under V. Raghavan in 1956. He served as Lecturer in Sanskrit at the National Sanskrit University, attested in 1965.
P. T. Narasimhachar worked in Indology and other fields. He studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1923–1927), where he was taught by Mysore Hiriyanna.
P. V. Ramanujaswami was an Indologist who served as Director of the Sri Venkateswara Oriental Research Institute, attested in 1944 and 1954.
